      - id: meta
        name: Calculate release metadata
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          git fetch --tags
          latest=$(git tag -l 'V*' --sort=-v:refname | head -n 1)

          if [ -z "$latest" ]; then
            latest="V0.0.0"
          fi

          base_version=${latest#V}
          IFS='.' read -r major minor patch <<< "$base_version"

          # ── Apply version bump (shared by official AND nightly) ──
          case "${{ inputs.bump }}" in
            major)
              major=$((major+1))
              minor=0
              patch=0
              ;;
            minor)
              minor=$((minor+1))
              patch=0
              ;;
            patch)
              patch=$((patch+1))
              ;;
          esac

          release_type="${{ inputs.release_type }}"

          if [ "$release_type" = "official" ]; then
            tag_name="V$major.$minor.$patch"
            release_name="Houdoku $tag_name"
            app_version="${tag_name#V}"
            prerelease="false"
          else
            nightly_stamp="$(date -u +"%Y%m%d-%H%M")"
            nightly_display="$(date -u +"%d/%m/%Y %I:%M %p" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')"

            # Keep git ref safe while exposing a friendly release title.
            tag_name="nightly-$nightly_stamp"
            release_name="Nightly - $nightly_display UTC"
            app_version="$major.$minor.$patch-nightly.${GITHUB_RUN_NUMBER:-0}"
            prerelease="true"
          fi

          echo "tag_name=$tag_name" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "release_name=$release_name" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "app_version=$app_version" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "prerelease=$prerelease" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

Now let me verify the complete file looks correct:The fix is complete. Here's a summary of what was wrong and what changed:

## Root Cause

In the `meta` step of `release.yml`, the version bump logic (`case "${{ inputs.bump }}"`) was **only inside the `official` branch**. The nightly (`else`) branch used `$base_version` directly — the raw latest tag version — completely ignoring the user's bump selection. So "Nightly" + "Major" produced `2.17.10-nightly.317` instead of `3.0.0-nightly.317`.

## Fix

Moved the version bump calculation **before** the `if official / else nightly` split so it applies to both paths:

| Scenario | Before (broken) | After (fixed) |
|---|---|---|
| Official + Major | `3.0.0` ✓ | `3.0.0` ✓ |
| Nightly + Major | `2.17.10-nightly.317` ❌ | `3.0.0-nightly.317` ✓ |
| Nightly + Minor | `2.17.10-nightly.317` ❌ | `2.18.0-nightly.317` ✓ |
| Nightly + Patch | `2.17.10-nightly.317` | `2.17.11-nightly.317` ✓ |

## Cross-platform

The change is **pure bash** in the `meta` step (which runs on `ubuntu-latest`), so it doesn't affect the Windows/macOS build jobs. The `app_version` output feeds the `Sync app version to release tag` step which uses Node.js (cross-platform) to update `package.json` before building. No platform-specific issues.

## No lint/release errors

This is a workflow YAML change only — no code changes to the application. GitHub Actions will parse the YAML just fine, and the bash logic is standard `set -euo pipefail` with proper arithmetic.
